epics.title: Core Experience and Identity
epics.jtbd: When a visitor lands on the site, I want to immediately understand the author's focus and have clear ways to contact them, so that I can explore their work or get in touch.
requirements: R1: The site's canonical domain is configured as dmitrii.eneik.com, and social profile links (LinkedIn, GitHub) correctly point to Dmitry Efremov's real profiles without placeholders.
R2: The interface uses natural Russian terminology (Связь, Написать напрямую, Заявка на сотрудничество) across all contact components, completely avoiding the term intake.
R3: A visitor can submit a direct message or collaboration request through an on-site form, saving the request directly to the site's database.
R4: A visitor receives an immediate, clear on-screen delivery confirmation when their message is successfully submitted, without being redirected to third-party tools.
R5: A visitor whose submission fails due to validation or connection issues retains their typed data and sees a clear error message.
R6: The system automatically sends an email acknowledgement to the sender upon submission of an enquiry, stating what was received and what happens next.
R7: The site includes an Impressum (Imprint) accessible from every page, detailing the legal entity, address, and contact information.

slices.title: Database schema for direct contact messages
slices.jtbd: When implementing contact form storage for this epic, I want a structured schema, so that visitor messages are safely persisted.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a database migration, When executed, Then it creates a table for contact messages with fields for sender, content, and timestamp.
Given the migration run, When queried, Then the table is correctly structured.

slices.title: Shared API contract for contact submissions
slices.jtbd: When implementing the contact flow for this epic, I want a shared OpenAPI contract, so that frontend and backend build against the same schema.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the OpenAPI spec, When updated, Then it defines the contact POST endpoint with request and response schemas.
Given the spec, When validated, Then it adheres to OpenAPI 3.0 standards.

slices.title: Backend endpoints for contact submissions and email acknowledgement
slices.jtbd: When implementing message handling for this epic, I want a secure endpoint to receive submissions and send emails, so that messages are processed.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a valid POST request to the contact endpoint, When processed, Then it saves the message and returns a success payload.
Given a successful save, When processing completes, Then it dispatches an email acknowledgement to the sender.

slices.title: Contact form UI and identity components
slices.jtbd: When implementing the contact form and identity for this epic, I want an interactive and accessible UI, so that visitors can submit messages and view correct links.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the contact page, When a user submits the form successfully, Then they see an immediate success message without redirection.
Given a validation error, When the error occurs, Then the typed text remains in the form.
Given WCAG 2.1 AA requirements, When testing the form, Then all form controls are labelled, keyboard operable, and meet 4.5:1 text contrast.
Given the footer, When rendered, Then social links point to Dmitry Efremov without placeholders and the Impressum is accessible.

slices.title: QA validation for contact flow and identity
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA for this epic, I want automated tests covering the contact flow, so that visitors can reliably submit messages.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the full stack, When E2E tests run, Then they verify the contact form submission succeeds and shows a confirmation.
Given the integration layer, When tests run, Then they verify API validation logic and email dispatch mocking.
Given the UI, When visually tested, Then the Impressum link and Russian terminology are confirmed present.

epics.title: Sovereign Canon and Ontology Architecture
epics.jtbd: When a visitor explores the site, I want to read the Evergreen manifestos and ontology across structured domains, so that I understand the core architectural philosophy.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Time on conceptual navigator pages > 2 minutes
requirements: R1: A visitor can interactively search and filter the knowledge base to find relevant author patterns and concepts.
R2: A visitor can navigate the site via a conceptual navigator that surfaces related ideas instead of just chronological posts.
R3: A visitor can interact with utilitarian applied models directly within the interface as functional tools rather than static text.
R4: A visitor viewing the knowledge base on a mobile device has a fully usable layout without horizontal scrolling or hidden controls.
R5: A visitor with an active search or filter sees a clear empty state if no results match, with an option to reset filters.

slices.title: Database schema for knowledge base
slices.jtbd: When implementing knowledge base storage for this epic, I want a structured schema, so that concepts and models can be queried efficiently.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a database migration, When executed, Then it creates tables for knowledge base concepts, tags, and applied model configurations.
Given the migration run, When queried, Then indices are created for search performance.

slices.title: Shared API contract for knowledge base
slices.jtbd: When implementing the knowledge base APIs for this epic, I want a shared OpenAPI contract, so that frontend and backend build against the same endpoints.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the OpenAPI spec, When updated, Then it defines the endpoints for fetching concepts, searching, and filtering.
Given the spec, When validated, Then it adheres to OpenAPI 3.0 standards.

slices.title: Backend endpoints for knowledge base search and retrieval
slices.jtbd: When implementing knowledge base logic for this epic, I want efficient search and retrieval endpoints, so that the conceptual navigator can render data quickly.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a search query, When calling the search endpoint, Then it returns matching concepts with applied filters.
Given a request for a concept, When called, Then it returns the structured manifesto content or model configuration.

slices.title: Conceptual navigator and interactive search UI
slices.jtbd: When implementing the conceptual navigator for this epic, I want an interactive UI, so that visitors can explore manifestos and search concepts intuitively.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the knowledge base page, When searching for a term, Then it dynamically updates the view with results.
Given no search results, When active, Then a clear empty state with a reset filters option is displayed.
Given a mobile viewport, When rendered, Then the layout adapts without horizontal scrolling and touch targets are usable.

slices.title: Applied models interactive UI components
slices.jtbd: When implementing applied models for this epic, I want interactive functional components, so that visitors can use the tools directly on the page.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an applied model on a page, When interacted with, Then it calculates or updates state functionally rather than displaying static text.
Given WCAG 2.1 AA requirements, When testing the model, Then keyboard navigation and ARIA labels are fully supported.

slices.title: QA validation for knowledge base features
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA for this epic, I want automated tests covering the search and models, so that visitors can reliably interact with the ontology.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the knowledge base, When E2E tests run, Then they verify the search filter applies correctly and empty states appear.
Given the applied models, When tested, Then they verify the functional logic works accurately and handles mobile layouts.

epics.title: Public API for External AI Agents
epics.jtbd: When an external AI agent operates on behalf of a user, I want it to securely read documentation, place service orders, and send direct messages, so that the user can seamlessly hire me or contact me through their personal assistant.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: API success rate for valid agent requests > 99%
requirements: R1: External AI agents can discover the site's capabilities by fetching /.well-known/ai-agent.json and /llms.txt manifests.
R2: External AI agents can fetch structured, machine-readable representations of the author's unique patterns and context via an OpenAPI-documented REST API.
R3: External AI agents can submit structured direct messages and collaboration requests on behalf of their users via the API.
R4: API requests from agents receive clear structured error responses (e.g., 400 Bad Request with validation details) if the payload is invalid.
R5: The API uses rate limiting to handle traffic from autonomous agents and prevent abuse.

slices.title: Shared API contract for AI agent capabilities
slices.jtbd: When implementing AI agent access for this epic, I want a formal API contract, so that agents can correctly format requests.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the OpenAPI spec, When updated, Then it includes the machine-readable content endpoints and agent submission endpoints.
Given the spec, When validated, Then it adheres to OpenAPI 3.0 standards and is publicly accessible.

slices.title: Backend manifests and machine-readable endpoints
slices.jtbd: When implementing agent infrastructure for this epic, I want discovery manifests and robust endpoints, so that autonomous agents can interact with the site.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a request to /.well-known/ai-agent.json, When served, Then it returns a valid JSON manifest detailing agent capabilities.
Given a request to the agent submission API, When sent with invalid data, Then it returns a 400 response with structured validation details.
Given high-frequency requests, When processed, Then rate limiting applies and returns a 429 Too Many Requests status.

slices.title: QA validation for AI agent APIs
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA for this epic, I want automated integration tests covering the agent endpoints, so that external integrations are reliable.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the API endpoints, When integration tests run, Then they verify structured error responses for invalid payloads.
Given the rate limiter, When tested under load, Then it correctly blocks excessive requests.
Given the manifest URLs, When fetched, Then they return valid configurations.
slices.tocConstraintRef: Mocking high traffic for rate limits

epics.title: Data Protection and Recovery
epics.jtbd: When the database experiences a failure, I want to be able to restore the system state from a backup, so that I do not lose my published content.
requirements: R1: The database holding contact messages and knowledge base data is backed up automatically on a regular schedule.
R2: A database restore from a backup is actively performed and verified in a staging or CI environment, confirming data integrity.

slices.title: Automated database backup and restore verification
slices.jtbd: When implementing data protection for this epic, I want scheduled backups and automated restore tests, so that data loss is prevented.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the production database, When the schedule triggers, Then an encrypted backup is securely stored.
Given a backup file, When the CI restore job runs, Then it successfully mounts the backup and verifies data integrity.
Given the restore job, When executed, Then automated tests pass verifying tables are intact.

epics.title: Data Subject Rights and GDPR Compliance
epics.jtbd: When a user whose personal data was submitted by an AI agent requests access or deletion, I want to be able to export or erase their data within the statutory deadline, so that the system complies with privacy regulations.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Time to fulfill data requests < 72 hours
requirements: R1: A visitor whose personal data was collected via the contact form can request an export of their data.
R2: A visitor can request the complete erasure of their personal data from the system, executed within the statutory deadline.

slices.title: Backend data operations for GDPR export and erasure
slices.jtbd: When implementing privacy tools for this epic, I want automated scripts or endpoints for export and deletion, so that statutory deadlines are met.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a request to export data for an email address, When processed, Then a structured JSON of all associated records is generated.
Given a request to erase data, When executed, Then all associated personal data is permanently deleted from the database.
Given the erasure process, When automated tests run, Then they verify the data is no longer retrievable.

epics.title: Privacy Consent Management
epics.jtbd: When a visitor arrives on the site, I want to be asked for consent before any non-essential trackers load, so that my privacy preferences are respected and the site complies with ePrivacy regulations.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Consent prompt display rate = 100% for new visitors
requirements: R1: A visitor arriving on the site is prompted for opt-in consent before any non-essential cookies or trackers load.
R2: A visitor can refuse consent as easily as accepting it, and their choice is recorded and revocable via a persistent settings control.
R3: Consent management is provided by an established CMP platform rather than a hand-rolled banner.

slices.title: Integration of CMP for privacy consent
slices.jtbd: When implementing consent management for this epic, I want to integrate an established CMP, so that privacy preferences are reliably enforced.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a new visitor on the site, When they land, Then the CMP banner blocks all non-essential scripts until consent is given.
Given the banner, When refusing consent, Then it is exactly one click, matching the acceptance flow.
Given the integration, When automated tests run, Then they verify cookies are not set before consent.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero non-essential cookies set before consent

slices.title: QA validation for privacy consent
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA for this epic, I want automated tests covering the consent banner, so that visitors' privacy preferences are reliably enforced.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a new visitor on the site, When E2E tests run, Then they verify the CMP banner appears and blocks non-essential scripts.
Given the banner is declined, When tests run, Then they verify no tracking cookies are set.
Given the banner is accepted, When tested, Then they verify scripts load correctly and consent is recorded.

epics.title: Platform Telemetry and Measurement
epics.jtbd: When operating the site, I want to measure visitor engagement with my content and external links, so that I know if the site successfully drives interest in my work.
requirements: R1: The site captures telemetry indicating the goal: whether the site successfully drives direct contact and agent interaction.
R2: The site answers the question: 'How many visitors and agents successfully submit a collaboration request?' by tracking form and API submission metrics.
R3: The site answers the question: 'Which conceptual navigator paths and applied models drive the most engagement?' by tracking knowledge base interaction events.

slices.title: UI and API telemetry instrumentation
slices.jtbd: When implementing measurement for this epic, I want event tracking on key interactions, so that the platform's goals can be evaluated.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the contact form and agent API, When a successful submission occurs, Then a conversion event is dispatched to the analytics provider.
Given the conceptual navigator, When a user searches or interacts with a model, Then an engagement event is logged with the context.
Given a visitor who refused consent, When they interact, Then no personal tracking telemetry is dispatched.

slices.title: QA validation for telemetry tracking
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA for this epic, I want tests covering event dispatch, so that measurement data is accurate and compliant.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given E2E tests, When a conversion action occurs, Then the test intercepts network requests to verify the telemetry payload.
Given a declined consent state, When testing actions, Then the test verifies no telemetry payloads are dispatched.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Telemetry test coverage = 100% for critical events

epics.title: Initial Content and Acceptance
epics.jtbd: When receiving the delivered system, I want to see it populated with realistic content, so that I can verify all paths and features work end-to-end.
requirements: R1: The delivered system is populated with realistic initial content in the author's domain, avoiding fake stubs or 'lorem ipsum'.
R2: The initial content includes a functional applied model and at least two conceptual knowledge base entries to allow full traversal of the navigation and filter paths.
R3: A complete traversal of the knowledge base search and contact submission is performed on the deployed instance to verify it works end-to-end.

slices.title: Realistic seed data for knowledge base
slices.jtbd: When implementing initial state for this epic, I want realistic seed content, so that the knowledge base is fully demonstrable upon deployment.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a fresh database, When the seed script runs, Then it populates the system with real-world author concepts and an applied model configuration.
Given the seeded data, When the site loads, Then the content is fully navigable without fake placeholders.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero broken links in seeded content

slices.title: End-to-end acceptance walkthrough
slices.jtbd: When verifying the deployed system for this epic, I want a complete traversal script, so that the acceptance floor is satisfied.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the deployed instance with seed data, When the acceptance suite runs, Then it successfully searches the knowledge base, interacts with a model, and submits a contact form.
Given the completion of the suite, When the results are logged, Then the entire user journey is confirmed operational on production-like infrastructure.
